text:
Wyrmwood Reserve reintroduced pine marten on Tuesday, releasing 14 animals from a three-year breeding program led by North Vale Ecology and the reserve authority. The first cohort, fitted with collar tags, was moved into 4,800 hectares of mixed conifer and broadleaf habitat after a final health check at the reserve’s Carrick station. Officials said the species had been absent from the site for more than 80 years.

Early monitoring suggests three individuals have already established feeding ranges along the Alder Run corridor. The program cost 1.9 million crowns, partly funded by timber operators. For the sector, the move strengthens the case for biodiversity-linked land management as a condition for future forestry permits.
